title: Minimally invasive in vivo endoscopic monitoring of dextran sulfate sodium-induced murine colitis
author: Bullard, Mundo, et al.

steps.title: Safety warning
steps.instruction: DSS induces epithelial cell breakdown when ingested; follow the Material Safety Data Sheet for correct handling and storage.

steps.title: Measure water consumption
steps.instruction: During the 7‑day acclimation period, record how much water each mouse (or cage) drinks per day, noting strain and number of mice per cage.

steps.title: Calculate weekly DSS volume
steps.instruction: Using the measured daily water intake, calculate the total volume of DSS solution needed for the upcoming 5‑ to 7‑day DSS cycle.

substeps.instruction: Use the desired w/v % concentration to determine the amount of DSS and water required.
For example, to make a 4 % DSS solution, dissolve 1.2 g DSS in 30 mL tap water.

steps.title: Prepare DSS solution
steps.instruction: Weigh the calculated amount of DSS and add it to the calculated volume of tap water.

steps.title: Mix solution in fume hood
steps.instruction: Stir the DSS‑water mixture inside a fume hood until fully dissolved.

steps.title: Aliquot into tubes
steps.instruction: Dispense each day's prepared solution into large conical tubes, one set per mouse cage.

steps.title: Store solution
steps.instruction: Place all conical tubes in a refrigerator set to 4 °C until use.

steps.title: Administer and replace DSS
steps.instruction: After the acclimation period, add the appropriate volume of DSS solution to each cage’s water bottle.

substeps.instruction: Keep the DSS‑filled bottle for three days.
After three days, replace with fresh DSS solution and thereafter change the solution every two days until the DSS cycle is complete.

steps.title: Set up heating pad
steps.instruction: Attach the heating pad to the water heater and turn the heater on to 42 °C.

steps.title: Connect air pump
steps.instruction: Plug in and turn on the air pump for the setup.

steps.title: Wrap Kimwipe around pad
steps.instruction: When the heating pad reaches temperature, wrap a large Kimwipe around it.
